records.name: AC Fairhill
records.summary: A youth soccer and fitness program in North Philadelphia that serves low-income kids. Camps, practices, and weekly community service trips are the main activities, and volunteers help with rides, gear, and snacks.
records.what_you_do: Kids take part in soccer camps and practices. Volunteers chaperone trips and collect equipment and donations. Coaches and trainers help out at camps and practices on a volunteer basis.

schedule.text: Camps, practices, and weekly community service trips. Days, times, and months are not published on the site.

locations.label: Practice field at 12th and Cambria streets (per a 2023 news story)

cost.text: Many families pay nothing. In a July 2023 news story a co-founder said the most any family pays is $75 for the year.

first_step.how: Email the group to ask about camps and practices. The site has a volunteer page; the sign-up steps are not stated.
first_step.basis: Camps and practices are described, but the site does not say how a family signs up, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group's own site has no dated posts. Status is dormant because the newest dated item is a July 2023 news story, even though the site looks current. Ages 4 to 16 and the $75 figure come from the 2023 story, not the site. The news story calls the group Athletic Club of Fairhill. Nonprofit status is not stated; the site calls it a philanthropic youth organization. The Programs page on the site was not readable.

records.name: Athletic Development Group
records.summary: A nonprofit that trains student athletes in basketball, football, soccer, and track and field, and adds academic support, health education, and leadership work. Families sign up by contacting the group.
records.what_you_do: Athletes train with certified coaches and get help with schoolwork, health education, leadership, and guidance on name, image and likeness. Families are invited to enroll, support the mission, or partner with the group.

schedule.text: Days, times, and months are not published on the site.

cost.text: Not stated. The site shows donation and store links but no program fees.

first_step.basis: The site invites families to enroll, but it gives no start dates, tryout rules, or age groups.

The newest dated item is a 2025 achievement with no month, so status is unknown. The site lists a Community Impact program with no join details. Copyright footers were not used as evidence.

records.name: Bicycle Coalition Youth Cycling (BCYC)
records.summary: A cycling team program for teens ages 12 to 18, run by the Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia. Riders start in a Core program at partner sites, then can move up to All Star teams in road, mountain bike, race, triathlon, or cyclocross.
records.what_you_do: Riders go to practices and events such as group rides, and can join a youth advisory council. Volunteers help at events, join practices, and help keep athletes' bikes in shape. The group pays its coaches and does not require racing experience for them.

schedule.text: All Star teams run in summer and fall. Practice days and times are not published on the page. The Philly Bike Ride is listed for Oct 18, 8:30 am to 1 pm; the year is not written beside it.

cost.text: Not stated for athletes. The scholarship listed is for program graduates after high school and is funded by donations.

first_step.how: Submit the online youth application; staff follow up about team placement
first_step.basis: Youth apply through a public online form, but the page does not say beginners are welcome in those words.

records.notes: The September recap's date line has no year. The year 2026 is taken from the same item's headline, which honors 2026 award winners. The eight partner sites are not named. Volunteer background check and training requirements are not stated. The phone number is the group's general line.

records.summary: A nonprofit that works to get Black women and girls into sport. Its youth work includes after-school sports programming, and the group also lists triathlon activity and a scholarship program.
records.what_you_do: Youth take part in after-school sports, such as fencing and lacrosse, according to a November 2025 news item. The site also has a volunteer page, but the roles on it are not stated.

records.name: Calvary Athletic Association
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia youth sports association with in-house and travel teams in baseball, softball, basketball, football, cheer, volleyball, and lacrosse. Young kids can start in in-house programs at age 3.

records.name: Chestnut Hill Youth Sports Club

records.what_you_do: Players try out for travel basketball. Volunteers can coach, manage teams, maintain fields, run the snack bar, or serve on the board. All coaches must submit Pennsylvania clearances, which are valid for 5 years.

schedule.text: Travel basketball has two tryout sessions; the dates are on the registration link. Travel soccer moves to school-year age bands starting with the 2026 to 27 season. Intramural basketball dates are not yet listed.

records.name: Fast Break Philly
records.summary: A girls' sports group in Philadelphia that runs fall volleyball clinics for 3rd to 8th graders and Sunday ultimate frisbee clinics. Clinics are sold by the session, and the site lists a community rate.

records.name: LEGACY Youth Tennis & Education
records.summary: A tennis and education program based at the LEGACY Tennis Center on Ridge Avenue. It offers junior clinics, camps, private lessons, tournaments, and after-school programs.

records.name: Leveling the Playing Field (Philadelphia)
records.summary: A youth sports charity that collects donated sports equipment and gives it free to kids who need it. Volunteers sort and check gear at a Philadelphia-area warehouse.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers book a shift of about two hours to sort and inventory donated gear, check that it is in good shape, and keep the warehouse in order. Individuals and groups may sign up. Volunteers must be at least 10, and an adult must be with anyone under 15.

schedule.text: The drop-off bin is open 24 hours outside the warehouse. Volunteer shifts are booked by appointment. Pick-up needs prior approval. Days and months of operation are not stated.

cost.text: Equipment is free for kids who need it. The site has an application page for families; application requirements are not stated.

first_step.how: Families use the Apply for Equipment page. Volunteers book a shift on the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: Both volunteering and applying have a clear online route, and the page says prior knowledge of gear is preferred but not required.

records.notes: The warehouse is in Sharon Hill, Delaware County, outside the city, and the page calls this the Philadelphia chapter. The pick-up email link goes to a different address than the one shown, so the Philadelphia address is recorded. No phone number is stated.
